title: Emotion
identity: The Philharmonie de Paris saxophone guide identifies Dautremer’s Émotion as a 1969 alto saxophone and piano piece in two parts: Andante in 4/4 at quarter=72, then a triple-meter poco scherzando in 6/8. The printed tempo for the second section is described as slow; the guide lists the piece at 3:15 and the range from low B to high E, without specifying written or sounding pitch convention.

evidence.claim: Guide entry gives date, sections, meter, tempos, duration and range descriptor.
evidence.source_name: Philharmonie de Paris, 10 ans avec le saxophone

evidence.claim: Lemoine/retailer edition metadata gives E-flat saxophone and piano, HX24250, and a publisher/vendor “easy” descriptor.
evidence.source_name: Sheet Music Plus, Lemoine edition listing

review_focus: Inference: the guide’s contrast between a measured Andante and a scherzando in 6/8 gives a concrete point for reviewing tempo transition and articulation.
collection_flag: Published original saxophone-and-piano work; guide entry provides a focused technical study description.
gaps: Guide does not state whether its range is written or concert pitch.
No score notation or recording inspected; retailer’s “easy” label is not a SaxoBrain level.
